quote:
To our knowledge this is:

1. **The first pangenome-scale systematic test** of the housekeeping-vs-adaptive copy-number-constraint hypothesis across bacterial phyla.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report tested 24 bacterial species across 5 phyla with a uniform pipeline built on the KBase Data Lakehouse, whereas prior work by Pushker, Gevers and Lalanne tested individual related-bacterium pairs or single organisms.
quote: Prior work (Pushker, Gevers, Lalanne) tested individual pairs of related bacteria or single organisms; we test 24 species across 5 phyla with a uniform pipeline built on the BERDL Iceberg lakehouse.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: To its knowledge, the report provides the first demonstration that the bacterial functional-class copy-number effect concentrates in accessory clusters.
quote: 2. **The first demonstration that the class effect concentrates in accessory clusters.** Papers that have reported "housekeeping genes are single-copy" have not, to our knowledge, decomposed the effect by core-vs-accessory pangenome status to show that the class × status interaction is much stronger than either main effect alone (adaptive-accessory is 25× adaptive-core, vs 5× housekeeping-accessory to housekeeping-core).
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report says the bacterial class × core-status interaction is much stronger than either main effect alone, with adaptive-accessory 25× adaptive-core versus housekeeping-accessory 5× housekeeping-core.
quote: Papers that have reported "housekeeping genes are single-copy" have not, to our knowledge, decomposed the effect by core-vs-accessory pangenome status to show that the class × status interaction is much stronger than either main effect alone (adaptive-accessory is 25× adaptive-core, vs 5× housekeeping-accessory to housekeeping-core).
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report operationalizes bacterial multi-copy rate as SUM(multicopy_genomes) / SUM(carrier_genomes), describing the weighted metric as robust to sparse, rare paralog-expansion events in bacterial pangenomes.
quote: 3. **A weighted-metric operationalization** (SUM(multicopy_genomes) / SUM(carrier_genomes)) that is robust to the sparse, rare-event nature of paralog expansion in bacterial pangenomes.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: Binary any-multi-copy flags underestimate the bacterial copy-number class effect by ~6× at pilot scale.
quote: Binary "any multi-copy" flags — the naive choice — underestimate the effect by ~6× at pilot scale.
heading: Novel Contribution

text: The report's gene-copy-number analysis uses motupan clusters at 90% AAI, merging recent paralogs diverged <10% while separating ancient paralogs diverged >10%, so it captures operationally recognized rather than phylogenetically complete paralogs.
quote: The gene clusters we count come from motupan at 90% AAI. Recent paralogs that have diverged <10% will be merged into a single cluster and their copy number will be counted. Conversely, ancient paralogs that diverged >10% appear as separate clusters and their functional relatedness is lost.
heading: Limitations

text: Fragmented metagenome-assembled genomes can inflate or deflate the report's multi-copy counts, with contig artifacts entering per-cluster-per-genome metrics linearly.
quote: Fragmented MAGs can split a single paralog family across contigs, inflating multi-copy counts, or merge them, deflating. Our per-cluster metrics are per-cluster-per-genome counts, so contig-level artifacts leak in linearly.
heading: Limitations

text: The report does not condition its copy-number analysis on checkm_completeness or contig N50 and says a tightest-quality-genome robustness analysis would strengthen the claim.
quote: We do not currently condition on `checkm_completeness` or contig N50; a robustness pass on the tightest-quality genome subset would strengthen the claim.
heading: Limitations

text: The report selected 24 bacterial species for 50–300-genome coverage, oversampling clinically important and well-studied taxa.
quote: The 24 species were selected for 50–300-genome coverage, which oversamples clinically important and well-studied taxa.
heading: Limitations

text: The report covers the top 5 phyla by candidate count—Pseudomonadota, Bacillota, Bacteroidota, Actinomycetota, and Campylobacterota—but excludes CPR, Patescibacteria, Spirochaetota, and archaea from that coverage.
quote: The 5 phyla we cover (Pseudomonadota, Bacillota, Bacteroidota, Actinomycetota, Campylobacterota) are the top 5 by candidate count but leave out CPR, Patescibacteria, Spirochaetota, and archaea entirely.
heading: Limitations

text: The report retained the Spirochaetota pilot species Borreliella burgdorferi but flagged it as a multi-partite-genome outlier whose plasmid-borne duplication raises housekeeping and adaptive rates together and breaks the direction test.
quote: The Spirochaetota pilot species (*Borreliella burgdorferi*) was retained but flagged as a multi-partite-genome outlier — its housekeeping rate is anomalously high because plasmid-borne gene duplication in this species affects housekeeping and adaptive categories together, breaking the direction test.
heading: Limitations

text: The report's coarse functional partition assigns housekeeping categories {F, H} to ~5% of species-level rows and adaptive categories {L, V, M, K} to ~15%.
quote: Housekeeping = {F, H} covers ~5% of species-level rows; adaptive = {L, V, M, K} covers ~15%.
heading: Limitations

text: Roughly 80% of clusters are classified as other and excluded from the primary copy-number test, so the report does not automatically extrapolate the tested class effect to all bacterial genes.
quote: Roughly 80% of clusters fall into "other" (poorly annotated, mixed, or intermediate function) and are excluded from the primary test. The class effect is real for the tested rows, but the extrapolation to "all bacterial genes" is not automatic.
heading: Limitations

text: The report does not test direct positive selection on copy number and considers housekeeping dosage-imbalance purifying selection, adaptive-paralog neutral tolerance with some positive selection, and proximity to mobile elements as alternative explanations.
quote: **We do not test for direct positive selection on copy number.** Our observations are consistent with either (a) purifying selection against dosage imbalance for housekeeping paralogs, or (b) neutral tolerance for adaptive paralogs plus positive selection on some of them, or (c) mechanistic bias (adaptive genes physically near mobile elements).
heading: Limitations

text: The report says distinguishing its alternative copy-number mechanisms requires dN/dS on paralog pairs and mobile-element context data.
quote: Distinguishing these would require dN/dS on the paralog pairs and mobile-element context data.
heading: Limitations

quote: | `kbase_ke_pangenome` | `gene`, `gene_genecluster_junction`, `gene_cluster`, `genome`, `eggnog_mapper_annotations`, `pangenome`, `gtdb_species_clade` | Gene-to-genome-to-cluster mapping (billion-row 3-way join); COG functional annotations; pangenome metadata for species selection; core/accessory flags on clusters |
